title: List of Forms and Contact Details Required to Request Medical Records From Brigham and Women's Hospital (2026)
summary: A 2026 guide to Brigham and Women's Hospital medical record forms, ROI contacts, Massachusetts copy fees, and authorization tips for personal injury law firms.
body_markdown:
Requesting medical records from Brigham and Women's Hospital (BWH) means working with Mass General Brigham's centralized Release of Information (ROI) service, plus separate contacts for images, bills, and chart corrections. For personal injury attorneys, knowing which form to use and where each piece of the record lives can save a lot of back-and-forth with corrected authorizations and missing materials. Law firms looking to take this off their plate can use[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) for AI-powered medical record retrieval that checks authorizations before submission and keeps following up until records arrive.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


BWH uses MGB's centralized ROI service for standard requests, while some MGB organizations have separate procedures


-


The ROI unit is reachable at 617-726-2361 (phone) or 617-726-3661 (fax), and authorizations go by mail or fax, not email


-


For a HIPAA access request, the hospital generally must provide access or issue a written denial within 30 calendar days, with one 30-day extension allowed under specific notice conditions


-


Effective October 1, 2026, Massachusetts maximum copying rates are a[$30.68 base charge](https://www.mahima.org/ma-medical-record-copy-fees) , $1.03 per page for the first 100 pages, and $0.53 for each additional page


-


Radiology reports can be requested through ROI, but image or film copies go through BWH imaging, and hospital bills go through Billing Customer Service


-


Incomplete or invalid authorizations can delay processing, and Codes Health's AI review helps reduce preventable rejections before submission


## **Understanding Your Rights: How to Request Your Own Medical Records**


### **Online Portals: Instant Access to Your Health Information**


BWH patients can view test results, visit summaries, and clinical notes through the Mass General Brigham Patient Gateway portal. Patients can also request records through Patient Gateway using Menu > Request Records. Records displayed in the portal may differ from the full scope available through an access request.


For litigation, the portal is a helpful starting point for reviewing what's available and spotting treatment dates, but it's not a substitute for a complete records request.


### **Paper Requests: When Digital Isn't an Option**


Patients who can't use the portal, or who need older records, can submit a written authorization. The[current BWH form](https://www.massgeneralbrigham.org/content/dam/unified-xwalk/documents/en/patients-visitors/medical-records-release-bwh-english.pdf) (marked 06/24) asks for:


-


Full legal name (including maiden name if applicable)


-


Date of birth


-


Current mailing address and phone number


-


Medical record number, if available


-


Date ranges for the requested records


-


Types of records needed (office visits, lab results, radiology reports)


-


Recipient information for third-party releases


-


Patient signature and date


The form expires six months after signing unless a different timeframe is specified. Keep copies of every authorization you send for follow-up.


## **Navigating the Process: Brigham and Women's Hospital Medical Records Request Form**


### **Where to Find the Official Form**


BWH's authorization is available in multiple languages through the Mass General Brigham[medical records page](https://www.massgeneralbrigham.org/en/patients-visitors/resources/becoming-patient/medical-records) . The English version is a downloadable PDF you can fill in electronically or by hand.


If your client was treated at more than one MGB hospital, such as Massachusetts General Hospital and BWH, use the consolidated MGB/Partners authorization rather than treating the BWH form as interchangeable. MGB lists separate instructions for some organizations, so check the page before you submit.


### **Key Sections to Complete Accurately**


These are the sections that most often need attention:


**Patient Identification Section**


-


Full legal name


-


Date of birth and current contact information


-


Medical record number, if available


**Records Specification Section**


-


Date ranges for the records you need


-


Types of records requested (check all applicable boxes)


-


Delivery method preference


Mail or fax the authorization; do not email the records request. Secure email may be selected for delivery.


**Authorization Section**


-


Patient signature (or an authorized representative's signature with documentation)


-


A signed, dated, unexpired authorization


-


Expiration date (optional; defaults to six months)


### **Avoiding Common Request Delays**


Incomplete or invalid authorizations can delay processing and require correction. Determine the applicable deadline based on the request's legal basis, since an authorization-based disclosure isn't the same as a patient's own access request. Common errors include:


-


Missing or illegible patient signatures


-


Incomplete date ranges that leave records unspecified


-


Sensitive record categories left unaddressed in Section D


-


Expired authorizations reused from earlier requests


-


Incorrect recipient information for third-party releases


## **Contacting the Records Department: Phone Numbers and Other Contact Details**


### **Centralized Mass General Brigham Contact Information**


BWH uses MGB's centralized ROI service for standard requests; some organizations have separate procedures.


**Primary ROI Contact Information:**


-


Phone: 617-726-2361


-


Fax: 617-726-3661


-


Mailing Address: 121 Inner Belt Road, Room 240, Somerville, MA 02143-4453


**BWH General Inquiries:**


-


Phone: 617-732-5500 (main hospital line)


**Hospital Bills:**


-


For hospital bills, contact Billing Customer Service at 617-726-3884. MGB notes that its Medical Records Department can't provide hospital bills.


### **Imaging and Radiology Records**


Request radiology reports through ROI. For image or film copies, contact BWH imaging at 617-732-7180; fax 617-732-5300.


This split catches a lot of requesters off guard. A standard records request can cover written radiology reports, but the actual images need their own request to the imaging department.


### **Chart Correction Requests**


Patients who find errors in their records can request corrections here:


-


Phone: 857-282-9736


-


Fax: 857-282-8110


-


Email: HIMChartcorrection@partners.org


The hospital generally must act within 60 days, with one permitted 30-day extension. If it denies the amendment, it must explain why and describe the patient's right to submit a disagreement statement, under[45 CFR § 164.526](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-E/section-164.526) .


## **Retrieving Older Records: How to Get Old Medical Records From Brigham and Women's Hospital**


### **Understanding Record Retention Periods**


Massachusetts hospital medical records generally have a 20-year minimum retention period following discharge or final treatment. Certain underlying materials, including radiological images, have a five-year minimum when their interpretive reports are retained in the medical record, under[105 CMR § 130.370](https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/massachusetts/105-CMR-130-370) . These are minimum periods, not a guarantee that BWH keeps every historical item.


When requesting older records, include specific dates of service to help the facility locate archived materials.


### **Special Procedures for Archived Information**


Older records stored off-site may take longer to pull. For a HIPAA access request, the hospital generally must provide access or issue a written denial within 30 calendar days. One additional 30-day extension is allowed if written reasons and a completion date are provided before the initial deadline. A few practical steps help:


-


Give specific dates of service for archived records


-


Ask whether an extension notice applies to your request


-


Ask for an itemized estimate of any applicable charges


### **Accessing Records from Previous Hospital Affiliations**


BWH has gone through organizational changes over the decades, including its integration into Partners HealthCare (now Mass General Brigham). Ask ROI whether records from the relevant treatment dates and predecessor facility remain available and who holds them.


## **HIPAA Compliance: Ensuring Secure and Authorized Medical Records Release**


### **Your Rights Under HIPAA**


Under the[HIPAA access rule](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-E/section-164.524) , the hospital generally must provide access or issue a written denial within 30 calendar days of a patient's access request. One additional 30-day extension is allowed if written reasons and a completion date are provided before the initial deadline.


Patients also have the right to:


-


Receive records in their preferred format (paper or electronic) if readily producible


-


Direct copies to third parties


-


Request an accounting of disclosures made by the hospital


-


File complaints with the HHS Office for Civil Rights if access is denied improperly


### **Elements of a Valid HIPAA Authorization**


A valid HIPAA authorization under[45 CFR § 164.508](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-45/subtitle-A/subchapter-C/part-164/subpart-E/section-164.508) includes, among other things:


-


A description of the information to be disclosed


-


Identification of who may disclose the information


-


Identification of the authorized recipients


-


The purpose of the disclosure


-


An expiration date or event


-


The right to revoke, and how to do it


-


Statements about conditioning of treatment and potential redisclosure


-


Signature and date, plus a description of a representative's authority where applicable


The simplest approach is to complete the current official BWH form rather than relying on an abbreviated checklist.


### **Releasing Records to Third Parties**


For routine law-firm retrieval, obtain an appropriate patient authorization unless another lawful disclosure pathway applies. Requirements differ for treatment, payment, and other permitted disclosures.


## **Third-Party Requests: Medical Records Release for Legal Needs**


### **Requests from Legal Firms and Litigators**


Personal injury attorneys requesting records for clients should submit a signed patient authorization that names the law firm as recipient and states the purpose (for example, "personal injury litigation").


Legal requests typically include:


-


A signed, dated, unexpired patient authorization naming the firm as recipient


-


An optional cover letter on firm letterhead, unless ROI requests one


-


Date ranges relevant to the case


-


A separate request to Billing Customer Service for hospital bills


### **Sensitive Record Categories Requiring Special Authorization**


Certain record types need explicit consent beyond a standard release. Complete Section D of BWH's form for applicable sensitive records. Additional consent or legal restrictions may apply. Categories include:


-


HIV test results ([Massachusetts HIV statute](https://malegislature.gov/Laws/GeneralLaws/PartI/TitleXVI/Chapter111/Section70F) )


-


Substance use disorder treatment ([42 CFR Part 2](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-42/chapter-I/subchapter-A/part-2) )


-


Mental health treatment records


-


Genetic testing information


-


Sexual assault counseling records


-


Social worker records


-


Domestic violence counseling records


If a sensitive category isn't authorized, those records may be left out of the release even when the date range covers the relevant treatment.

## **Massachusetts Medical Record Fees**


Knowing the fee rules helps with case budgeting. Effective October 1, 2026, the published Massachusetts maximum copying rates under[Massachusetts records law](https://malegislature.gov/Laws/GeneralLaws/PartI/TitleXVI/Chapter111/Section70) are:


-


Base charge: $30.68


-


Pages 1 to 100: $1.03 per page


-


Pages 101 and up: $0.53 per page


**Cost Examples** (assuming the state schedule applies and excluding any other lawful charges):


-


50-page ER record: $82.18


-


200-page hospital record: $186.68


Applicable federal patient-access restrictions may require lower charges. For patients requesting electronic copies of electronically maintained records, a provider may use an optional flat fee of up to $6.50 or another permitted cost-based calculation, per[HHS fee guidance](https://www.hhs.gov/hipaa/for-professionals/faq/is-650-the-maximum-amount-that-can-be-charged/index.html) . Confirm the applicable charge before ordering.


Distinguish requests for patients' own copies from requests directing delivery to a law firm. Different fee rules can apply. Ask for an itemized estimate of any applicable charges.


The Massachusetts fee exemption applies to requests made solely to support qualifying Social Security or financial-needs-based benefit claims, and reasonable supporting documentation may be requested.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the typical turnaround time for medical record requests from Brigham and Women's Hospital?**


For a HIPAA access request, the hospital generally must provide access or issue a written denial within 30 calendar days, with one 30-day extension allowed if written reasons and a completion date are provided before the initial deadline. Authorization-based requests to a law firm may follow different rules, so confirm the expected timing with ROI. Codes Health reports a general average turnaround of a couple of weeks and helps reduce preventable authorization rejections through pre-submission review.


### **Can I request medical records for a family member at Brigham and Women's Hospital?**


Yes, if you have the patient's authorization or applicable representative authority. Parents can generally request a minor child's records, with exceptions for certain minor-consented care, and a guardianship order isn't universally required. For incapacitated adults, a healthcare proxy or court-appointed guardian provides supporting documentation. For deceased patients, an executor or administrator of the estate can request records with appropriate legal documentation.


### **What should I do if I believe my medical records from BWH are incomplete?**


Compare the delivered records against your original request to pin down the gaps. Contact the ROI unit at 617-726-2361 about missing materials. If images are absent, confirm that a separate request went to BWH imaging at 617-732-7180, and request hospital bills from Billing Customer Service at 617-726-3884. Document all communications and follow up in writing if problems persist.


### **Is there a fee for requesting medical records from Brigham and Women's Hospital?**


There can be. Effective October 1, 2026, Massachusetts maximum copying rates are a $30.68 base charge, $1.03 per page for the first 100 pages, and $0.53 per page after that. For patients requesting electronic copies of electronically maintained records, a provider may use an optional flat fee of up to $6.50 or another permitted cost-based calculation. Different fee rules can apply when records go to a law firm. The fee exemption applies to requests made solely to support qualifying Social Security or financial-needs-based benefit claims.


### **How do I request radiology images from Brigham and Women's Hospital?**


Request written radiology reports through ROI. For image or film copies, contact BWH imaging at 617-732-7180 (phone) or 617-732-5300 (fax), and make sure your authorization covers the images you need.
